result:
Fixed and verified — `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (7 tests, including the 5 new ones) both pass, and `bunx guren check` reports 0 failures.

The vulnerability was in `PostController.update` (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:88`), which took the raw `await this.request.json()` and passed it to `Post.forceUpdate()` — bypassing both the Zod payload schema and the model's `fillable` allowlist, so any key in the request body (`authorId`, `createdAt`, an empty `title`) was written straight to the row. I replaced that with `const data = await this.validateBody(PostPayloadSchema)` followed by `Post.update({ id: post.id }, data)`, mirroring how `store` validates: the schema enforces `title`/`excerpt`/`body` (required, 255/500 caps) and returns a 422 with field errors before anything is written, strips keys outside those three, and `update` rather than `forceUpdate` keeps `authorId` — deliberately absent from `Post.fillable` — unreachable from request input. The existing `authorize('update', ...)` check is untouched, so non-authors still get a 403. I added `tests/PostUpdate.test.ts` covering the happy path, the author-hijack attempt, an empty title leaving the post unchanged, an out-of-form `createdAt` being ignored, and the non-author 403.
